value.why: First-inning scoring distribution baseline.
The first three batters, not the whole lineup, decide the first inning.
Confirmed top-three hitters and order.
Handedness of top-order hitters vs starter.
Starter quality in the first trip through the order.
Early walks and zone rate: walks arise when pitchers miss the zone and hitters take pitches outside it; both the pitcher's command and the lineup's discipline matter.
K% reduces baserunners: strikeouts occur when a pitcher's swing-and-miss and called-strike ability meet hitters prone to striking out; lineup K% by handedness captures the hitter side.
Later-inning markets depend on trip through order.
Bullpen entry for later innings.
Run environment: park dimensions, altitude and surface change run, HR and hit probabilities for both teams, and by batter handedness.
Temperature and wind: temperature, air density and wind change ball flight, so fly-ball outcomes (HR, doubles) vary with conditions.
Early-game zone effect: the home-plate umpire's called zone determines strike/ball outcomes on borderline pitches, changing strikeouts, walks and run scoring.
Inning-level distribution: runs per team per game are overdispersed and inning-clustered, so threshold and total markets depend on distribution shape and the correlation between teams.

Rules for called games (Fair Price if the inning is not completed), the 9th-inning no-bottom-half wording and the RFI one-line rule; the inning strikes listed run innings 1-9, so no extra-innings clause is relevant.
BABIP luck in the starter's recent first innings regresses; raw first-inning ERA overstates persistent skill.
Replaces first_inning_splits as a computational estimand and removes dependence on 30-start samples.
The ninth is a state-conditional, non-exchangeable inning; no existing catalog input captures the skipped-bottom and closer selection.
Provides the base rate by inning index and a ceiling for how much inning-specific tendency is real.
The plate-appearance simulation propagates base-out states across innings so each inning-index strike gets consistent run probabilities (stage s2).
Weather delays and called games drive the Fair Price branch of every inning market (stage s5).
Reference-class frequency: for off-field markets, history of similar announcements is the best available prior.

Timestamped league, venue and schedule-leak reports about whether the 2027 special-event game is staged and which clubs are named; reports precede the official announcement, so a report's timestamp relative to market close and its source matter (player and team-strength news is irrelevant to this contract).
Resolution wording and source.

Price reaction to schedule leaks and announcements: the traded price aggregates participants' information about staging and the pairing, so large moves ahead of the official release signal leaked information; read it with mlb.news_source_reliability_score.
Liquidity affects quote reliability.
Close time vs event timing: market open, close, halts and postponement events determine when information can be traded on and which pregame snapshot is the last valid one.
Other venues' prices where they exist.
Base rates by market type: realized frequency by rung gives the unconditional base rate that every conditional model must beat, and reveals persistent biases in how thresholds are set.
KXMLBFODTEAMS resolves all clubs No if no 2027 game is announced with participants or played, so staging is the first multiplier.
Gives each KXMLBFODTEAMS club market a probability that respects the two-participant constraint and regional selection pattern.
A lockout after the Dec 1 2026 CBA expiry can delay the 2027 schedule release or cancel the event, sending every club market to No.
Leaks about participants precede the official announcement and must be weighted by each source's historical reliability.
Current leaderboard and games remaining.
Rate x opportunity projection per contender.
Qualification thresholds for rate stats.
True-talent rate for hitters: a hitter's quality per plate appearance (on-base skill, power, contact quality) determines hits, bases, runs and RBIs.
True-talent rate for pitchers.
Opportunity (PA/IP) projection.
Injury risk to contenders: absences change lineup/rotation composition and late scratches can void or reprice player markets.
Regress hot streaks in HR totals.

BBWAA-class ballot history only (MVP, Cy Young, Rookie, Manager of the Year): points scales, ballot timing and finalist announcement; other electorates are in award_electorate_procedure and award-specific inputs.
WAR and counting stats voters see.
Team outcomes correlate with votes.
Stat source and settlement date.
The probability a player finishes first is the probability his final total exceeds every rival's; correlations and games remaining set it.
Provides the estimand the voter hypotheses refer to and distinguishes finalist from winner markets.
Defines the candidate set for the ROY market, a first-order determinant of probabilities.
The finalist rule gives a No branch tied to the announcement calendar, so its probability must be estimated.
Gives a specific input for the monthly and weekly awards filed in this archetype, otherwise unaddressed.
Triple Crown is rare, so the joint distribution is crucial.
Defines the selection process for the All-Star series that previously had no stage or input.
Defines the joint structure for combination markets.

Manager of the Year (KXMLBALMOTY, KXMLBNLMOTY, filed here) is a BBWAA vote cast before the postseason that rewards wins over preseason expectation; this is the manager-specific score used in stage s7.
The archetype mixes BBWAA awards with panel, beat-reporter, fan and executive votes; the electorate decides which voter model and which training data apply to each series.
KXMLBALHAARON and KXMLBNLHAARON settle on an award partly decided by fans; the panel-only production model misprices popular candidates.
KXMLBEOTY (moved here) settles on the executives' award, which none of the BBWAA, fan or manager inputs measures.
KXMLBTEAMSTAT (team strikeouts leader) is a thirty-staff order statistic computed by this engine.
Single-hitter season thresholds filed here (50 HR, 50 HR plus 40 SB) are tails of the joint power-speed season distribution.
The playoff leader and series MVP markets (stage s6) depend on how many playoff games and plate appearances a player gets.
The team strikeout leader (stage s8) is batters faced times each staff's strikeout rate.
Team strikeout and season threshold races (stage s8) need games remaining and totals to date.
Series MVP markets (stage s6) are the team series-win probability times the player credit share.

Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (interaction on mlb.team_season_extreme_engine x mlb.k_rates x mlb.deadline_roster_strength_shift: A staff's strikeout lead depends on who pitches the remaining innings: a deadline acquisition of a high-strike) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.
Pre-registered statistics-based narrative flags (milestone, comeback, first-year, positional scarcity, team surprise) enter the vote models as terms fitted per electorate.

Reliever of the Year (KXMLBALRELOTY/KXMLBNLRELOTY) is a reliever-only electorate decision; this gives the candidate pool its saves, leverage and WPA features, which award_stats_war (generic WAR/counting) does not.

value.hypothesis: Velocity decline and injury tend to arrive together, so a falling trend lowers both the ceiling and the expected remaining exposure; treating them as independent overstates the probability for declining candidates.
value.how_to_test: Test whether a velocity z-score drop in the last three appearances predicts a 60+ day IL stint within 30 days, controlling for age and workload.

value.hypothesis: Park speed offsets bias a candidate's measured ceiling depending on where he pitches; a closer whose home park reads hot appears closer to the threshold, and the contract settles on that biased reading.
value.how_to_test: Compare candidates' home and road 99th-percentile speeds after removing league-wide park offsets estimated from visiting pitchers.

value.hypothesis: When the best candidate ceilings sit more than about 2 mph under the line the physical exceedance probability is near zero and the anomaly rate sets P(YES); only when a candidate's ceiling approaches the line does the physical tail dominate, so the weight on each route switches with the ceiling gap.
value.how_to_test: Across seasons, compare the count of live-feed readings above 105 mph that survive in corrected Savant data against the count of physical pitches above 104.5; check which grows with ceiling gap.

value.hypothesis: The three nested thresholds change regime: where the threshold is inside the observed tracked range the exceedance probability is an empirical frequency times exposure and is driven by a few named arms; where it is beyond the observed range it is a bounded-tail extrapolation driven by the assumed endpoint, so pool size and exposure matter differently by threshold and the three any-pitcher events must be modelled jointly with P(107+) <= P(106+) <= P(105+).
value.how_to_test: For each threshold T, count Statcast pitches at or above T per season and by pitcher, compare the empirical exceedance frequency with the GPD-extrapolated one for the pool, and check monotonicity across 105, 106 and 107.

value.hypothesis: Season exceedance is roughly 1 - exp(-N x p): N near-peak pitches times the per-pitch tail p given the ceiling. A pitcher topping out 3 mph below the line has p near zero, so even thousands of pitches add nothing; exposure only matters for arms whose ceiling is close.
value.how_to_test: Across 2015-2025, regress whether a pitcher's season max exceeded his prior-season 99.9th percentile by 1 mph on log near-peak pitch count interacted with distance from that percentile.

value.hypothesis: A starter moved to the October bullpen switches from paced effort to max effort, raising his top-speed distribution by one to three mph for the remaining appearances; regular-season starter exposure says little about this regime.
value.how_to_test: Compare within-pitcher 99th-percentile fastball speed in postseason relief versus regular-season starts for starters used in relief in 2015-2025 postseasons.

value.hypothesis: An additive lift (leverage, rest, temperature, all fixed effects inside the lift input) shifts the per-pitch distribution, and because the threshold sits in the bounded tail, tail probability rises convexly with the lift until close to the endpoint.
value.how_to_test: Count pitches above each pitcher's personal 99.9th percentile by temperature and leverage bins; check that the ratio grows faster than the mean speed shift.
